problem_markdown: A convex quadrilateral has area $32$. Two opposite sides and one diagonal have total length $16$. Determine the possible length of its other diagonal.
solutions_markdown:
Label the quadrilateral $ABCD$ so that $AB+CD+AC=16$, and put $AC=x$. The perpendicular heights of $B,D$ from $AC$ are at most $AB,CD$. Thus
$$32\le\frac{x(AB+CD)}2=\frac{x(16-x)}2\le32.$$
Equality forces $x=8$, $AB+CD=8$, $AB\perp AC$ and $CD\perp AC$. The horizontal and vertical components of $BD$ therefore both have length eight, giving $BD=8\sqrt2$. Conversely, any positive $AB,CD$ summing to eight in this perpendicular configuration gives a convex quadrilateral with the required area, so this value is attained.
